news.title: Inside the life of Veerle Buurman
news.body_en: This season, we will be catching up with Chelsea players to give you even more insight into some of your favourite stars. The next to sit down with us is talented defender Veerle Buurman... Where did you grow up, and what was it like there? I grew up in a place called Bemmel. It was a really nice village. I grew up with my younger brother and older brother, and my parents. It was a really good life there. What age did you first start playing football? I started playing when I was five years old. What was the name of your first grassroots team? It wasn't really a formal team at first. I started playing with two of my best friends and we trained every Wednesday. Eventually, it called F15. How old were you when you first joined an academy? I played for 12 years with the boys at my village club, SC Bemmel. Then I joined the youth team at PSV and was there for about six months before moving into the first team. Who would you say has been the biggest influence on your football career to date? What's your biggest career highlight to date? Playing for the national team, being at Chelsea, my time at PSV and, of course, my early days at Bemmel. So everything really! Who are your best friends in football? I have quite a lot of friends. At Chelsea, I'm really close with Liv, Sio and Mika. Outside of Chelsea, I have friends from PSV like Lisan [Alkemade], Emma [Frijns] and Moon [Pondes]. Can you name your top three favourite players of all time? Virgil van Dijk is my idol because of his playing style as a centre-back. And, of course, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are incredible players who have inspired me. In England, they call me Vee. In Dutch, it's Veer or Veertje, which is an affectionate version of my name. What do you like to do most away from football? I love spending time with good people and doing nice things. Outside of football, things that you always want to do but sometimes when you are within football you can't. And also being with my family and friends. Are you watching any TV series at the moment you could recommend? If we looked at your Spotify playlist, who would be dominating your most-played artists? I listen to a mix of everything, but Olivia Dean is definitely one of my favourites. What are your top three holiday destinations? In Europe I really like Spain and Italy. I really want to visit Greece as well and also Portugal which I would really like to surf one day. If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them? I'd probably make some nice wraps and tacos. What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? From my parents, it's to keep both feet on the ground and believe in yourself. What does football mean to you? Everything. I love football. I have a lot of fun both on and off the pitch. Laughing and enjoying the game is the most important thing for me.

news.title: What kit are Chelsea wearing against Fulham?
news.body_en: It's almost time for our first Premier League fixture of the new season as we prepare to take on Fulham, and it's time to find out what the Blues will be kitted out in! Chelsea are back in competitive action on Monday night with the short trip across west London to face Fulham at Craven Cottage. After an extensive pre-season programme, Xabi Alonso's side are ready for the challenge of beginning the 2026/27 campaign against our local rivals in the first of Chelsea's Premier League fixtures this season. Supporters can follow all the action from Craven Cottage across the Chelsea Official App and website, where you will find Chelsea live updates, match coverage and post-match reaction throughout the evening. Kicking off at 8pm UK time on Monday, Chelsea will be kitted out in our new 2026/27 Nike home shirt, with the Blues wearing our traditional colours for the opening Premier League fixture of the season. Central to the kit's design is the club crest, which has been refreshed and interwoven proudly in 'Bright Blue' in the fabric on the front of the shirt. There is a collar and a button-down neck, and 'Midwest Gold' accents for the rampant lion badge and Nike swoosh, which feature on both the jersey and the shorts. news.title: Xabi Alonso backs ‘world-class’ Cole Palmer to shine this season
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has described Cole Palmer as 'world class' and believes the forward can produce his very best football this campaign after enjoying a full pre-season under the new Chelsea head coach. Palmer heads into the new season in a strong position after spending the summer working under Alonso from day one of pre-season at Cobham, and the Blues head coach is excited by what he has seen from the attacker ahead of our Premier League opener against Fulham on Monday night. The 24-year-old has already established himself as one of the most influential attacking players in the division since arriving at Stamford Bridge, and Alonso believes the conditions are now in place for Palmer to enjoy another standout campaign. ‘Cole is determined to enjoy his football,’ said the Chelsea manager. ‘He wants to be fit. He wants to feel healthy. He wants to have a good connection with the players around him. And I've said that if we have this Cole and we are able to reach him and he feels that flow in the game and that he connects well with the players, I'm sure that his level is top-class, world-class I would say, and that he will have a great season.’ Those comments underline just how highly Alonso rates Palmer's ability, with the Spaniard confident the forward can reach the highest level when he is playing with freedom and confidence. Palmer has spent the entirety of pre-season working alongside his new head coach and team-mates, and has returned to Cobham recharged after enjoying a full off-season for the first time in four years, due to international competitions for club and country. With no international commitments during the summer, Palmer has been able to immerse himself fully in Alonso's methods from the outset, helping him build rhythm and understanding within the squad ahead of the campaign. He has also been joined by one of his closest friends in football, Morgan Rogers, following the attacking midfielder's summer arrival from Aston Villa. After seeing injuries interrupt his momentum at various stages last season, Alonso has been encouraged by Palmer's commitment to making sure those setbacks remain in the past. The Chelsea manager believes the experience has ultimately helped the attacker grow and develop a stronger understanding of his body. When asked if Cole's injury problems were behind him, Alonso replied: ‘Yes. I think that sometimes you need to go through a difficult moment with an injury or whatever to learn from that,’ 'I think that Cole has gone through a difficult period with the injury, and now he's working really hard to have the prevention not to have to feel those symptoms. ‘Since the first day, he's been working really hard to avoid that.’ Chelsea begin the Premier League season away to Fulham, and supporters can follow all the action live in our Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website, where you'll find minute-by-minute updates and live audio commentary. Fans can also experience the matchday through the new Chelsea Official App, where we will have an ongoing story from Craven Cottage.

news.title: Fulham vs Chelsea: All the key stats and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea begin our Premier League season with a west London derby on Monday evening. Ahead of our meeting with Fulham, we've pulled together all the vital facts, figures and statistics to get you ready for the Craven Cottage clash. Chelsea begin our Premier League season with a west London derby on Monday evening. In the match, Real Madrid's last two former managers will go head-to-head. Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa also played together for Liverpool in nine matches against Chelsea between 2007 and 2009. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition. Chelsea and Fulham are two of nine clubs to have new managers at the start of the Premier League season. Nine is the highest number in the competition’s history surpassing eight in 2016. The Blues (10th) and Fulham (11th) finished level on 52 points last season with only goal difference separating the sides. The Blues have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage with Fulham winning the other two. Our last draw there was in 2012. Fulham are seeking consecutive top-flight wins over Chelsea for the first time. Their only previous back-to-back victories against the Blues came between 1977 and 1979 in the Second Division. Only Man Utd (27) and Arsenal (26) have won more Premier League games against Fulham than Chelsea (23). Head-to-Head (all competitions) Chelsea 4-0 Fulham - 1925/26 & 1983/84 - both in Division Two Fulham 3-0 Chelsea - 1950/51 - FA Cup Chelsea’s biggest win at Fulham - 4-1 in 2004/05 in the Premier League Fulham’s biggest league win against Chelsea - 3-1 in 1976/77 in the Second Division This match begins the club's 35th Premier League season. We are one of six clubs to be ever-present in the competition. We have won 20 of our 34 Premier League opening-weekend matches, a win rate of 58.8 percent. Chelsea begin with six Premier League matches in London, with Everton on 17 October the first fixture requiring travel outside of the capital. Chelsea’s most recent opening-day away match was in 2022/23, when Jorginho’s penalty earned victory at Everton. That was also Chelsea’s last opening-weekend win, followed by two draws and one defeat. Xabi Alonso's first Premier League goal came against Fulham at Craven Cottage for Liverpool in October 2004. For the second season running, and the 16th time overall, we have begun a league campaign with a London derby. Twenty-seven Chelsea players have scored on their Premier League debut for the club, most recently Christopher Nkunku at Wolves in December 2023. Mick Harford was the first, against Oldham on the opening day of the inaugural Premier League season in 1992. The Blues have won four of our past five Premier League London derbies, losing the other. Reece James is the current Chelsea player with the most matchday one appearances for us in the Premier League (five). If selected, Danny Welbeck will become the first player ever to make a Premier League appearance for each of Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United. Finished 11th in the Premier League with 52 points. Lost 0-1 at home to Southampton in the fifth round of the FA Cup. Lost 1-2 at Newcastle in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup. Harry Wilson was Fulham's top scorer with 11 goals in all competitions. Fulham scored 47 Premier League goals last season, their lowest total in the competition since their 2020/21 relegation campaign, when they managed 27. Bernd Leno has played every Premier League match in each of Fulham’s past three seasons in the competition. The Cottagers have won three of their last four Premier League matches at Craven Cottage (one defeat). Fulham have won their opening game in one of their last six Premier League seasons (two draws, three defeats), beating Everton in 2023/24. They won three (Brentford, Chelsea, Tottenham) and lost three (Arsenal, Crystal Palace, West Ham) of their six home London derbies last season. The Cottagers have lost their previous three London derbies on the opening weekend of a Premier League campaign. Marco Silva left Fulham for Benfica in the summer after five seasons as head coach, following the expiry of his contract. Newly appointed head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has never managed a side against Chelsea. As a player he won two and lost four of the nine games against the Blues for Liverpool between 2007 and 2009. Wesley Fofana is suspended (two matches) following his second red card of the season against Sunderland on the final day of last season. Fulham’s Joachim Andersen is also suspended. Assistants: Adam Nunn, Dan Cook John Brooks refereed one Chelsea match last season: our January Premier League meeting with Brentford at Stamford Bridge.

news.title: Lacroix looking forward to start of a ‘beautiful season’
news.body_en: Maxence Lacroix can’t wait for his first season as a Chelsea player to begin and is hopeful of making it a memorable one for Blues supporters. Following his summer move across the capital from fellow Premier League side Crystal Palace, Lacroix made his first outing for Chelsea in last weekend’s friendly win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge. That was our final pre-season fixture before the real action begins with our Premier League opener away at neighbours Fulham on Monday evening. Having got his first taste of the action with his introduction to the Blues fans, our new defender can’t wait to get started in his first competitive match. ‘I really enjoyed my first game,’ said Lacroix. ‘I really enjoyed wearing the Chelsea jersey and also being in front of the fans. It was a good moment and we got a win, which was perfect for me! ‘I think everyone is looking forward to Monday and we have a big season in front of us, and it's starting in just a couple of days. ‘Of course, I know all about London derbies and Fulham. I knew them also with Palace, but I know that now with Chelsea, with this big club, it's also totally different, and I'm looking forward to all these derbies.’ Lacroix was one of the late-comers to pre-season training at Chelsea, after being part of the France side which reached the semi-finals of the FIFA World Cup over the summer. However, he has quickly settled in to his new surroundings and is already well accustomed to switching between defensive shapes, with Xabi Alonso having used both a back three and a back four during pre-season ‘I’ve settled in well, it’s been really good working with the manager and the other players,’ he added. ‘It’s really good. All the guys are good and it’s been top training with them every day. ‘I've played back three and I've played back four at Wolfsburg, at Palace and also in the national team. So for me it's all right for both tactics. ‘I think it’s important for any player to be able to play different ways. And also to understand how we want to play, that is always important for me.’ That leaves Lacroix ready and eager for the start of the 2026/27 season, which he hopes will be one to celebrate for those on the pitch and in the stands. ‘The big message for the fans is that it's going to be a beautiful season and we need you with us so we can enjoy it together.’

news.title: Under-18s report: Birmingham 1-4 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s secured our first points of the new Under-18 Premier League campaign with a convincing 4-1 victory away to Birmingham City. The Blues made a fast start in the West Midlands, with first-year scholar Isaac McGillvary opening the scoring after seven minutes. Heze Grimwade doubled our advantage shortly before half-time, however Birmingham were given a route back into the contest when Connor Reilly pulled a goal back just before the interval. The points were secured in the second half though, with Andrew Pennie netting a brace and securing our fine win. Chelsea took the lead in the seventh minute through McGillvary. The first-year produced a composed finish, taking one touch before finding the net to put the visitors 1-0 ahead. The young Blues continued to hold the advantage as the first half progressed and extended it five minutes before the break. Grimwade took a good touch before finishing neatly to make it 2-0, putting us in a strong position heading into the closing stages of the half. Birmingham responded immediately before the interval, with Reilly finishing well following a surging run from Blake Campbell, to reduce the deficit to 2-1 at half-time. Chelsea restored our two-goal advantage midway through the second half. Josh Henry produced the work which created the opening for Pennie, who was in the right place to finish and make it 3-1. Pennie struck again 10 minutes later to complete his brace. The ball dropped kindly for the forward and he made no mistake, giving the Blues a three-goal cushion. Pennie, who had been shifted from centre-forward to the left, continued to provide a threat and played a key role in our victory. There was still time for the visitors to threaten again. Jacob Dako saw a left-footed effort from outside the box blocked in the 77th minute, before Yunus Linton tried his luck from more than 35 yards six minutes later but fired over as the Blues saw out the game well. The result gives Chelsea our first points of the 2026/27 Under-18 Premier League campaign, following defeat to Norwich City in our opening fixture. Our Under-18s return to action on Wednesday when we play Wolverhampton Wanderers in the U18 Premier League Cup, in a 2pm kick-off. We will then be back at Cobham on Saturday 29 August when we host Reading in the Under-18 Premier League. That game will start at 11am. news.title: Joao Pedro picks his five special moments with Chelsea
news.body_en: Joao Pedro wasted no time making his mark during his first year at Chelsea, and after signing a new contract with the club, he has selected his favourite moments with the Blues so far. The Brazilian arrived from Brighton and Hove Albion last summer and went straight into the action as we triumphed at the FIFA Club World Cup in the USA. He then became a central figure in the team throughout the 2025/26 campaign. That contribution has been rewarded with a new contract until 2034 for the striker, who celebrated by choosing five of the games for Chelsea which have meant the most to him in his Blues career to date… I think in my first game, I was feeling very happy against Palmeiras, about making my debut. Like I said when we were on tour in Asia and Australia this summer, I didn't know before that Chelsea had a lot of fans in other countries like that. When I joined in America, I could see the passion they have for this club there. When I made my debut everyone was saying to me: "Congratulations, you’re very welcome here,". So I think my debut was very important for me. My first goal with Chelsea was against Fluminense, where I started my career. It was the first time since I moved to England that I played against them, so I got to see a few of my friends from when I was young, that I used to play with. So it was special for me, not to score against them specifically, but to achieve that moment. I was arriving at a big club. What I was doing – scoring my first goals for a big club against the team that gave me a lot – felt special. So I think that moment means a lot to me. The final of the Club World Cup was a special moment. We knew the game would be difficult because Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League and everything. But I think Cole had a special day. Me also, as I could score and I could help the team. I think at the back we are solid as well. So I think that day was Chelsea’s day. Everything was perfect and we could win. It was a very special moment for me. It was my first trophy as a professional player, so I cannot leave that out from my five best moments at Chelsea. Tottenham away was a great win with the fans in a derby atmosphere, and I got the winning goal. It was also because when I was at Brighton, I had lots of good moments against them too, so I enjoyed playing against Tottenham. Now I am at Chelsea and I know the rivalry is very big with Tottenham, so scoring the winning goal was even better, and it was a nice moment to celebrate with the fans after winning a derby. Against Napoli, I scored twice in the Champions League for the first time and I did it in a big game and a big atmosphere, which made it even more special. For me, to play in the Champions League is very important for me, because when I was young I always dreamed of playing for a big club and playing in big Champions League games. So scoring that winning goal for Chelsea was an important moment, not just for me, but I think for Chelsea too, because we had too many games and if we won that game we would finish high enough in the classification to qualify straight for the last 16.

news.title: Xabi Alonso thrilled ‘great personality’ Joao Pedro has signed new contract
news.body_en: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has spoken of his delight at seeing ‘leader’ Joao Pedro commit his long-term future to Chelsea. On the eve of our latest Premier League campaign – which starts on Monday evening with a London derby away to Fulham – the Brazilian penned fresh terms with the Blues that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034. And with the No.9 on his back for the season ahead, last season’s top scorer will be aiming to reach similar heights under Alonso, who has been delighted with the way the striker has applied himself in pre-season. ‘We talk a lot with Joao because he's not just a great player, but also a great person,’ Alonso said of the Brazilian international. ‘He has a great personality within the group. ‘I think that his development as a great player and as a leader is very noticeable every day, and in each game. He has this focus and this desire to have a great season, to score goals, but he is also focused on helping the team. ‘I'm very happy with Joao and with this news [signing a new contract]. I'm very impressed with his personality and now we need to help him in reaching his goals.’

news.title: Exclusive Interview: Joao Pedro
Highlights: Birmingham City U18s 1-4 Chelsea U18s
Joao Pedro signs new Chelsea contract
news.body_en: Chelsea is delighted to announce that Joao Pedro has signed a new contract until 2034. The Brazil international joined the Blues in July 2025 and made an immediate impact, scoring in the Club World Cup semi-finals and final as we were crowned world champions. Joao Pedro continued to be decisive in his first full season as a Chelsea player. He netted 20 goals in all competitions and ended the 2025/26 campaign as our supporters’ Player of the Season. ‘I am very happy to sign a new contract with Chelsea,’ Joao Pedro said. ‘I always dreamed of playing for a big club, and it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club. Chelsea has a long tradition of winning and it has big ambitions for the future. ‘I have a very good relationship with everyone here at the club and I have felt at home here in London from the moment that I joined. 'Everyone is very excited for this season. We know we can achieve a lot of things, we have a great team, we have a coach who wants to win and has won already. I am fully committed, everyone is ready and hopefully we can achieve our targets.' Signed from Brighton and Hove Albion, Joao Pedro quickly delivered for the Blues. He struck a brace against former club Fluminense to help us into the Club World Cup final, and then netted in our victory over Paris Saint-Germain as we claimed the trophy. His goalscoring form continued into his first full campaign in blue. He netted our opening goal of the 2025/26 season, away at West Ham United, and later scored the only goal in an away win over Tottenham Hotspur. Our new No.9 also had an impact on the European stage, with a fine brace netted in a victory over Napoli in the UEFA Champions League. Joao Pedro ended the campaign with 20 goals scored for the Blues, which saw him overwhelming voted as our Player of the Season. Congratulations on your new contract, JP!

news.title: Alonso on Palestra: 'He's something different'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes Marco Palestra’s talent, versatility and personality will make him an important asset for Chelsea throughout the 2026/27 campaign. Palestra joined the Blues this summer from Atalanta after being named Serie A's standout defender following a breakthrough season on loan at Cagliari. Palestra showcased his all-round ability as a full-back and a wing-back with the Sardinian club. But perhaps most impressively, he excelled on either side of the pitch to the extent many found it impossible to tell which was his preferred flank or stronger foot. That is a rare talent even at the top level of the game in England, as Alonso discussed when facing the media ahead of Monday night’s opening Chelsea fixture of the season away at Fulham. ‘I would say it's probably unusual in England because, in Italy for example, it's quite common, and he has had this education in Italian football to play both profiles,’ explained Xabi. ‘It doesn't matter if you are right-footed or left-footed, just that you are versatile. So he has this option, this energy. ‘He's something different, maybe not that common here, but in Italy it's quite common.’ However, it is not just Palestra’s versatility on the pitch which has impressed our manager, with the Spaniard quick to highlight the personality the defender has brought to Cobham and the positive effect he is already having on the squad before his competitive debut for the Blues. ‘He's had a great impact as well in the changing room,’ Alonso added. ‘He's integrated really well. He's a great guy and with this freshness that he has brought, apart from his football qualities, he's a very great addition to the club.’

Premier League 2 report: Bournemouth 2-1 Cobham Next Gen
news.body_en: Cobham Next Gen were beaten 2-1 by Bournemouth Dev Squad in our opening Premier League 2 fixture of the season, despite taking the lead through Reggie Watson's first-half penalty. Watson's spot-kick gave Chelsea the advantage before the interval, but Bournemouth responded through Jonny Day on the stroke of half-time and the forward struck again late on to secure all three points for the hosts. The young Blues created a number of chances throughout the evening and went close to restoring the lead after the break, with Harrison Bettoni particularly unfortunate not to get on the scoresheet. The Blues' starting line-up included four players who had travelled with the first team on our tour this summer, as Calvin Diakite, Tayo Subuloye, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli and Watson were all named in the side by Harry Hudson. Chelsea threatened early on when Leo Cardoso cut in from the right and saw a left-footed effort blocked. Chizaram Ezenwata then showed his strength to hold off a defender and collect Bettoni's pass, but his shot towards the near post was saved by the Bournemouth goalkeeper. The breakthrough arrived six minutes before half-time. Bettoni reacted quickest to reach Watson's deflected cross and was brought down inside the penalty area, with the referee pointing to the spot. Watson stepped up and confidently sent the goalkeeper the wrong way to open the scoring, marking his Premier League 2 debut with a goal. Chelsea's lead lasted until first-half stoppage time, when Bournemouth counter-attacked and Day cut inside before finding the net with a clinical right-footed finish from a central position. The Blues looked to regain the initiative after the restart. Nicoll-Jazuli dragged an effort wide before Cardoso tested the goalkeeper with a right-footed strike from the centre of the box. Bettoni was then denied by a smart save before coming within inches of putting Chelsea back in front. Watson's pinpoint cross found the forward inside the area, but his header struck the post and bounced clear. Subuloye also headed wide following a corner as Chelsea continued to push forward. The decisive moment arrived in the 89th minute, though, when Day was released and finished emphatically with a low right-footed drive to put Bournemouth ahead. Chelsea searched for a late equaliser and Bettoni had the final opportunity in stoppage time, but his effort drifted wide of the left post. news.title: Morgan Rogers: We’re confident of hitting the ground running
news.body_en: Chelsea have to wait until the very end of gameweek one to kick off our Premier League season. But when we do, Morgan Rogers believes the Blues are well placed to make a strong start. Our short trip to Craven Cottage to play Fulham on Monday evening follows the nine other fixtures on the opening weekend of the campaign and heralds a new dawn at Chelsea. Xabi Alonso is preparing to take charge of his first game as our manager and several new players – including Rogers – are hoping to make their competitive debut for the Blues. He may not have been at the Bridge for long, but Rogers is already acutely aware of the standards he and his team-mates are expected to meet. He wants to set the tone for the season right from the off. ‘There’s a process, and there being a new manager, it takes time to gel and fit perfectly, but we do want to hit the ground running,’ said Rogers. ‘We believe we've got the ability and the quality to. ‘The fans want to see their team perform to the level that they expect, and Chelsea Football Club as a whole expect to compete with every team and be right at the top of the league. That's our aspiration and goal. ‘It's about staying focused, and understanding it's a journey. It might not always go perfect, but with the right mentality, with the right mindset, we'll be where we deserve to be and where we need to be as a club and as a team.’ On a personal level, Rogers has been forming connections with his new colleagues as quickly as possible to ensure no time is wasted in getting up to speed. He has also taken information on board about what Alonso expects of him. What is unknown is how the Premier League will pan out this season. Several clubs, including us, Manchester City and Liverpool, have new head coaches. There is a feeling among pundits that it will be an open division and, as always, anyone can beat anyone on their day. ‘It’s exciting times ahead,’ Rogers enthused. ‘I'm as much of a Premier League fan as everyone else. I know I play in it, but I'm still a fan when I'm not playing. So I want as much excitement as possible. ‘No one knows how each team will set up or how everyone will play, and that’s exciting. That’s why we watch the game and why we love the sport. ‘And hopefully, we're in the exciting element of it at the top of the table where we want to be.’

Xabi Alonso on Levi Colwill's importance and place among world's best centre-backs
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes a fully fit Levi Colwill is 'one of the best centre-backs in the world' and insists our Academy graduate will be a key figure for the Blues during the forthcoming campaign. For much of the 2025/26 campaign, the Blues were deprived of Colwill's qualities due to a knee ligament injury sustained on the opening day of pre-season. Thankfully, the England international made a handful of appearances before our campaign was completed, and he has been working with Alonso’s squad since they reconvened at Cobham in July. Colwill featured during our tour of Australia and Asia and started on Saturday as we overcame Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge in our final pre-season fixture. With the start of the Premier League campaign almost upon us – we open with a short trip across west London to take on neighbours Fulham on Monday evening – Alonso has discussed Colwill’s return to full fitness and what the 23-year-old adds to the side. ‘I would say that having a proper pre-season has helped him in taking the right steps in the right moment, not trying to rush it too quick because of what he had last year,' said our manager. ‘Even last year, he finished playing in a good way. And now, after pre-season, we are expecting that he feels well and that he's confident and with the fitness to have him at the next level.’ That will be music to the Chelsea supporters’ ears, so impressive have Colwill’s performances been at the heart of the Blues defence before his injury. For Alonso, the defender’s potential importance to the team during the coming campaign is clear, too. ‘If he's feeling okay, he's for me one of the best centre-backs in the world, because of his composure, because of his presence. He’s so complete, so dominant. Levi is going to be a key player for us.’

news.title: Inside the life of Lucy Bronze
news.body_en: With the kick-off to Chelsea Women’s 2026/27 season fast approaching, we caught up with Blues and England defender Lucy Bronze, who extended her contract earlier this summer, to find out a bit more about her life off the pitch... Where did you grow up, and what was it like there? In the North-East of England, in Northumberland. I'd say it was very peaceful and quiet. It didn't feel like it, but it was very far away from anything, really. But it was the best; I played outside every day. Every sport, climbing trees, going to the beach. I had a very peaceful childhood and was very active. At what age did you first start playing football? Pretty much as soon as I could walk. At the age of five or six, my brother was always kicking a football around. I was two years younger –  three or four probably – and was playing, but I probably fell in love with it the most around the age of five or six. What was the name of your first grassroots team? How old were you when you first joined an academy? Who would you say has been the biggest influence on your football career to date? Probably my mum. From being in a village where there wasn't any access to girls' football, she and my dad took me everywhere, but my mum's the one who looked up everything. She didn't even really like football at the time, but she just wanted me to succeed in whatever it was I loved. What's your biggest career highlight to date? I think winning the Euros in England. Who are your best friends in football? My whole life, from the age of 12, I played with Lucy Staniforth. She has just retired this summer, but I think it would have to be her. Can you name your top three favourite players of all time? Marta, Mia Hamm, Rachel Yankey. What do you like to do most away from football? I’m either with my dog or just trying new food. Are you watching any TV series at the moment? I just started rewatching some of the Marvel series because, obviously, Spider-Man has been out, so I'm going back to watch some of the old Marvel movies. If we looked at your Spotify playlist, who would be dominating your most-played artists? At this moment, it's probably Bad Bunny. What are your top three holiday destinations, either that you've been to already or you would like to go to? I'd like to go to Brazil. Of the nice places I've been, Sardinia and Formentera. If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them? I was in Mexico this summer, so I learned how to make proper homemade tacos. Can you tell the fans something that they might not know about you? When I visit new places on holiday, I like to do cooking lessons. What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? What does football mean to you? Football means everything to me. It's how I've made friends and in the whole of my life because of football. So, I'd say close to everything, but not quite.

news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea Gameweek one
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Here, we look at which of the Blues' players are must-haves, who the best value-for-money picks are, and why Joao Pedro(£7.5) is Chelsea’s most popular player. Chelsea’s headline attacking addition, Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) has seen his ownership steadily increase above 25 per cent since starting and scoring against Real Sociedad last weekend. The Englishman has surpassed 160 points in each of the last two seasons, missing just two matches in that time and registering 37 attacking returns. Expected to play a key role on the left-side of the Blues’ attack and could form part of an attacking double-up. At the other end of the pitch Maxence Lacroix (£6.0m) looks set for a strong season at the heart of Chelsea’s backline. The Frenchman has risen in price after notching 154 points in 35 starts for Crystal Palace in 25/26, putting him eighth among defenders. Encouragingly, he returned DefCon points in over half of his appearances. Lacroix also provides attacking threat, racking up 23 shots from set-plays last season, the same amount as Arsenal’s Gabriel. Just like last season,Joao Pedro (£7.5m) is the highest-owned Chelsea player in FPL. The Brazilian currently sits in 62 per cent of teams, second among all players. Pedro’s pre-season form has caught the eye, scoring seven goals in five matches including a hat-trick against Western Sydney Wanderers and a brace at Stamford Bridge at Real Sociedad. Encouragingly for GW1, Chelsea’s new number nine has form against Fulham. In Gameweek 3 last season, Pedro scored the only goal of the game and notched maximum bonus points. Last season, the Brazilian returned 177 Fantasy points thanks to 15 goals and nine assists, his best-ever season across all three metrics. The under-lying data for Joao Pedro in 2025/26 was equally impressive. No Chelsea player managed more shots (73), big chances (26) or Expected Goals (14.96). Levi Colwill (£5.0m) returned to full fitness at the end of season and started in the Blues’ final friendly on the left of the back-three. In his limited Premier League game time in May, the Englishman averaged an impressive 10 DefCon p/90, hinting at potential for plenty of additional points. Only one of Chelsea’s first eight matches rank higher than three on the Fixture Difficulty Rating (FDR), increasing the potential for clean sheets. Likewise, in goal, Robert Sanchez (£5.0m) could provide value between the sticks this season. The Spaniard is owned by just 2 per cent of managers and has surpassed 100 points in each of the last two seasons. Erling Haaland(£15.5m) is likely to be the most captained player this weekend for Manchester City’s home match against Bournemouth. Last season’s Golden Boot winner racked up 239 points in 25/26 thanks to 27 goals, eight assists and 43 bonus points. The Norwegian has scored on the opening day of the season in each of his four seasons in the Premier League with three double-digit hauls in that time. Elsewhere, Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) could prove a shrewd choice for FPL managers. The Portugal international ended last season just four points behind Haaland following a stunning run of form under Michael Carrick. In the second half of the season, no player delivered more double-digit hauls. This stat showcases Fernandes’ explosive potential. With penalties and other set-pieces in his locker, an away match against newly-promoted Hull City should prove fruitful.

news.title: Alonso: 'James makes the team better wherever he plays'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has reiterated that Chelsea captain Reece James makes the Blues a better team no matter where he is deployed on the pitch. Having represented England at this summer's World Cup, James returned to Cobham at the start of last week to begin working with Alonso as our preparations for the forthcoming campaign continued. The 26-year-old featured in midfield during our final pre-season friendly of the summer – a 3-1 win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge – and will be in contention to play in our Premier League opener at Fulham on Monday evening. The Blues manager has the option to use James centrally in a back three, as well as at full-back, wing-back, or in central midfield. Yet whichever role the England international is handed in the weeks and months ahead, the quality of our skipper is undiminished. ‘He's flexible in his game, but he needs to feel important,’ said Alonso. ‘I think that's the main thing. Not just because of the role he has as a captain, but also because of the quality he gives to the rest of the team. ‘Wherever he plays, as a right-back or as a midfielder, normally he makes the team better because of his quality, because of his game intelligence, his experience, his composure with the ball. ‘So it's good that we have players that can play in different positions, not just him, other players as well. ‘I see him in a good mood, in a good mindset. For sure, the club means so much to him, and we want to have a good start, a fresh start with good momentum, and that's why the start is so important on Monday.’

news.title: Pre-Season Briefing 2026/27 part five: The anniversaries ahead
news.body_en: In the fifth and final part of our series building up to the new season, club historian Rick Glanvill picks out some Chelsea anniversaries we will be celebrating over the next nine months... • One-hundred-and-twenty years since Chelsea’s biggest ever league victory – 9-2 at home to Glossop in Division Two, with debutant ‘Gatling Gun’ George Hilsdon netting five. • Sixty years since a letter from supporter Clifford Webb published in the matchday programme on 7 September 1966 helped popularise a new name for the Fulham Road End at Stamford Bridge – ‘The Shed’. • Fifty-five years since Chelsea thrashed Luxembourg part-timers Jeunesse Hautcharage 13-0 in the Cup Winners’ Cup at Stamford Bridge on 29 September 1971 – completing a UEFA record 21-0 aggregate victory. • Ten years since Chelsea’s 5-0 Bonfire Night flaming of Everton at Stamford Bridge on 5 November 2016 was proclaimed the ‘best performance ever seen in the history of the Premier League’ by veteran commentator John Motson. • Five years since goals from Romelu Lukaku and Kai Havertz beat Palmeiras to earn Chelsea’s first Club World Cup crown on 12 February 2022. • Fifty-five years since the evergreen Chelsea anthem ‘Blue Is The Colour’ was released on Penny Farthing Records on 18 February 1972, reaching no.5 in the charts – unprecedented for a club song. • Twenty years since Didier Drogba’s brace against Arsenal on 25 February 2007 at the Millennium Stadium secured the fourth League Cup final victory in Chelsea’s history. • Seventy years since the first senior men’s match under floodlights at Stamford Bridge – a friendly against Sparta Prague on 19 March 1957. • One-hundred-and-twenty years since temporary manager William Lewis steered Chelsea to the club’s first-ever promotion to Division One with a 4-0 victory over Wolverhampton on 13 April 1907. • One hundred and fifty years since the opening of Stamford Bridge as an athletics venue on 28 April 1877, attended by a crowd of 6,000. • Fifteen years since Roberto Di Matteo’s team beat Liverpool 2-1 in the FA Cup final on 5 May 2012 with goals from Ramires and Didier Drogba. • Fifty years since the young and much-loved Chelsea team managed by Eddie McCreadie and led by Ray Wilkins clinched promotion back to Division One with a 1-1 draw at Wolves on 7 May 1977. • Ten years since Antonio Conte’s barnstorming first season in charge ends with Chelsea, powered by Eden Hazard, Diego Costa and Cesc ‘Magic hat’ Fabregas, winning the league for the sixth time at West Brom on 12 May 2017. • Thirty years since the dawn of a thrilling new era with superstar Ballon d’Or winner Ruud Gullit as coach began with Chelsea winning the FA Cup final against Middlesbrough on 17 May 1997 – our first major silverware for 26 years. • Fifteen years since the Blues’ Champions League triumph on 19 May 2012 at the home of Bayern Munich, who had unfurled pre-match banners proclaiming ‘Our city, our stadium, our trophy.’ We remain London’s first and only winners of the trophy. • Twenty years since Didier Drogba scored the winner against Man United on 19 May 2007 (pictured top) to complete Chelsea’s only FA Cup and League Cup double – we were the third club to complete the feat and the first to claim the FA Cup at the new Wembley (having been the last club to do so at the old stadium in 2000). • Sixty years since Tommy Docherty’s ‘Diamonds’ played the first ever ‘cockney FA Cup final’ at Wembley on 20 May 1967, losing 2-1. • Ten years since John Terry, Chelsea’s most successful youth product and captain, made his final appearance for the club at home to Sunderland on 21 May 2017.

Xabi Alonso delivers the latest Chelsea team news ahead of Fulham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has delivered the latest Chelsea team news ahead of our opening Premier League game of the season, with our manager stating he has no fresh injury concerns to contend with. The Blues kick-off the new season with a short trip along the Thames to take on London neighbours Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday evening. That game starts at 8pm and will be shown live on Sky Sports. Alonso sat down with the media on Thursday at Cobham, where he explained that Danny Welbeck should be fit to feature while the players who returned to pre-season late due to the World Cup are all available. ‘Danny can be involved, he just needed a couple of days not training that much because of a little thing,’ the Spaniard explained at his media briefing. ‘We expect him to be back [training] on Saturday. We need to go day by day, but that is the plan at the moment. ‘With the other players, let’s see. We will check and assess them, but for sure because of the World Cup they came back a little bit later and will need a little more time. ‘But they are all available and can be selected in the line-up against Fulham, for sure.’

news.title: Premier League ticket news: Hull at home
news.body_en: Ticket sales information has been released for our second home Premier League match of the season. The Blues host Hull City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday 12 September with a 3pm kick-off. Supporters intending to travel to or from this game using the London Underground are advised that planned engineering works may affect your journey. There will be no District Line service between Tower Hill and Edgware Road to Wimbledon, Kensington (Olympia), Richmond and Ealing Broadway stations. This means Fulham Broadway Station will be closed all day and there will be no District Line trains running to any nearby stations on that branch of the tube network. There is also no Circle Line from Edgware Road to Aldgate (via Victoria). Home tickets for members for men’s team matches are now allocated through a new application process. For each home match, eligible members have a designated application window during which they can apply for tickets. Applications can be made individually or as a group, provided all members of the group are eligible to apply during that window. Tickets will be allocated one per person with a maximum of four per application. Ticket application window opens – Friday 21 August 12pm Ticket application window closes – Wednesday 26 August 12pm The Ticket application window will be open for True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, and Junior Blue members. As part of the verification process, a pre-authorisation charge £0.01 will be applied to validate your payment card. No money will be taken at this stage, and the hold will be removed by your provider. Tickets for this match are priced at Category B. Please click here for match ticket prices Tickets will appear on the Chelsea Official App prior to the event. Eligible members can submit their application through the ticketing portal at any time during the window, supporters must ensure they are logged in to successfully apply. Applying earlier does not increase the likelihood of success, giving supporters greater flexibility to apply at a time that suits them. As part of the new ticket sales process, members who are eligible for concession-rate tickets are automatically assigned their price class. To ensure you are receiving the correct ticket, please take the time to check the date of birth on your account is accurate. You will only be allocated tickets in your selected areas unless you choose to be considered for other available options. If you only wish to be entered for tickets in one area of the stadium, please leave the second option blank. Please read the ticket application information carefully before submitting your application. Successful and unsuccessful applications will be notified by email within four working days of the ticket application window closing date. Successful applications will be charged to their payment card approximately at this time. Supporters are not able to use account credit for ticket application window purchases. Tickets are for Chelsea supporters only. All persons under the age of 16 will be required to attend with and sit next to, a person aged 18 years of age or over. Members and season ticket holders can purchase Westview tickets for Premier League home games via the Chelsea FC Official Ticketing Portal. A maximum of four tickets can be bought per person, and only the ticket purchaser is required to be a member or season ticket holder. You are not required to be a member or season ticket holder to purchase non-Westview Club Chelsea packages. Club Chelsea tickets are non-refundable unless the match is cancelled, postponed, or moved more than 48 hours either side of the scheduled fixture date. All Club Chelsea ticket purchases are subject to Club Chelsea terms and conditions. For any further Westview enquiries, please email clubchelsea@chelseafc.com. Loyalty points will now only be awarded for attendance at men’s first-team home matches and no longer accrued for purchasing tickets. Points will be added to eligible accounts following each game, provided the ticket has been scanned at the turnstile. This means that supporters purchasing tickets on the ticket exchange, or receiving tickets via ticket forwarding, will now receive loyalty points for attending matches. Supporters will receive three loyalty points for attending this match. Points will be applied after the fixture has been played. Members can still purchase general admission tickets if available in line with the General Admission Policy. Supporters who require accessible tickets can apply through the accessible ticket application window. Timings are below: Accessible ticket application window opens - Friday 21 August 12pm Accessible ticket application window closes – Wednesday 26 August 12pm Supporters, if they are able to do so, can call our Access Team on 0371 811 2012 or 0044 207 915 1950 (international callers) for any questions or if they need further information. Personal assistant tickets can be submitted during this ticket application window. Supporters can apply for car parking by clicking here from Friday 28 August You are required to display your Blue Badge while parked at Stamford Bridge. In addition to season ticket holders, True Blue+, True Blue and CFC Blue members now have the option to list tickets on the ticket exchange if they are unable to attend a home match. Supporters can access the ticket exchange through the Official Ticketing Portal. The sales information on the Buy Tickets page will be updated once the ticket exchange is open. The ticket exchange will close three hours before kick-off, unless stated otherwise. Those unsuccessful in the ticket application window will have a ticket exchange priority window. Once open, season ticket holders and members can send and receive tickets up until three hours before kick-off. Please note that those who have forwarded their ticket will not be able to list their ticket on the ticket exchange. Click for ticket forwarding FAQs Match and ticket application window dates are subject to change. All ticket sales are subject to availability. Please check the website for the latest information.

news.title: Chelsea FC Women announces partnership with Rimmel London ahead of inaugural season at Stamford Bridge
news.body_en: Chelsea FC Women today announces a new partnership with Rimmel London, bringing together a club and a brand united by a shared ambition to promote confidence and self-expression. Rimmel London will become an official partner of CFCW for the 2026/27 season, with the partnership seeing us work together across a range of initiatives designed to celebrate the club’s players, our passionate fanbase and the wider women’s football community. Rimmel London is the generation-defying cosmetic brand known for making beauty accessible and encouraging young people to feel confident. With a bold and youthful identity, Rimmel offers a wide range of products across face, eye, lips and nails while combining everyday affordability with on-trend beauty innovation. To kick off the partnership, Katie McCabe, Lauren James and Lucy Bronze all feature in a campaign to spotlight the Match Perfection foundation, designed to deliver long-lasting wear through every match-ready moment. Throughout the 2026/27 season, fans can look forward to Rimmel London bringing community experiences to CFCW home games, including a pop-up at the season opener against Aston Villa Women on 5 September which will be showcasing and sampling Rimmel London's Match Perfection foundation. Rimmel London will also be visible pitch side on the LED boards at every home game. Giulia Mazzia, commercial director for Chelsea FC Women, said: ‘We are thrilled to welcome Rimmel London to the CFCW family. This partnership is a fantastic opportunity to bring together the worlds of women’s football and beauty, while celebrating confidence, individuality and self-expression – all key values our players embrace. We look forward to working closely with the team at Rimmel London.’ Janine Fernandes, vice president of global marketing for Rimmel London, said: ‘Becoming Chelsea Football Club Women’s official partner for the 2026/27 season is an incredible moment for Rimmel, in our hometown of London. The club’s passion for female empowerment and resilience aligns to our values of self-expression and individuality, making our partnership a perfect match. Both brands have a deep cultural impact and influence with dedicated fan bases. By bringing them together, we have an exciting opportunity to grow and champion confidence, the power of self-expression with beauty and to celebrate the power of women both on and off the pitch.’ Further information on upcoming activities will be shared across CFCW’s channels throughout the season.

news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea's best buy, watch and differential
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. It’s difficult to look beyond Joao Pedro (£7.5m), who currently sits in over 60 per of FPL teams after a stunning pre-season. The Brazilian scored seven goals in five matches, including a brace in the Blues’ most recent victory over Real Sociedad. No Chelsea player registered more Expected Goal Involvement (xGI) than our new number nine, with a tally of 14.91.  Encouragingly for Gameweek 1, Joao Pedro netted against Fulham last season. With Manchester United and Liverpool midfielders proving popular due to favourable early fixtures, Cole Palmer (£9.5m) is very much one to watch in the opening Gameweeks of the season. The Englishman should benefit from a summer break and has racked up plenty of pre-season minutes. With penalties in his locker, Palmer could rocket in ownership with a strong performance on Monday night. With Xabi Alonso setting Chelsea up in a back-three formation for the final three pre-season friendlies, Fantasy managers will naturally be drawn to the attacking defenders. Marco Palestra (£5.5m), signed from Atalanta in the summer, has taken up some very advanced positions in pre-season and can play on either side. The Italian currently sits in just 2.7 per cent of Fantasy teams, making him a huge differential with routes to points at both ends of the pitch.

news.title: Rewarding our Official Supporters Clubs with enhanced benefits
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club has launched a refreshed offering for our Official Supporters Clubs, giving Blues around the world even more ways to feel connected to the club, wherever they are. The updated programme introduces a range of enhanced benefits for all official clubs, alongside the opportunity for all clubs to receive reward packages that recognise and celebrate their ongoing engagement and support. Under the refreshed Official Supporters Club Programme, all clubs, outside of ticketing clubs, will move to a single-tier structure, with access to a consistent package of benefits. Ticketing clubs can also access these rewards and benefits but their tiering remains unchanged. These include an official Chelsea Supporters Club wall flag, new certificate of affiliation and new official logo, as well as recognition on Chelsea’s Official Supporters Club website. Clubs will also have the opportunity to request Chelsea support for events and initiatives, receive exclusive content including a dedicated supporters club newsletter, website features and Official Supporters Club-only competitions, and gain access to global supporter events. Additional benefit packages will also be available to all recognised clubs. Through the refreshed rewards structure, Official Supporters Clubs can earn a range of recognition and experience-based benefits as their engagement grows. Depending on the package unlocked, clubs can receive additional items such as an Official Supporters Club pennant or scarves, Chelsea FC merchandise, signed items, exclusive virtual event access, priority access to global CFC events, CFC+ discounts, a player or legend message and even an exclusive matchday experience. More information on rewards and benefits, including FAQs, is available for all supporters to view The available packages, which are named after elements of the Chelsea FC crest, can be found below. 250 members registered on the official website 500 members registered on the official website 1,000 members registered on the official website 2,000 members registered on the official website 15 CFC members (True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, Junior Blue) 50 CFC members (True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, Junior Blue) 100 CFC members (True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, Junior Blue) 200 CFC members (True Blue+, True Blue, CFC Blue, Junior Blue) 5 photos posted of supporters club activities using #ChelseaFCOSC 10 photos posted of supporters club activities using #ChelseaFCOSC 15 photos posted of supporters club activities using #ChelseaFCOSC 15 photos posted of supporters club activities using #ChelseaFCOSC Official Supporters Club pennant 2 Official Supporters Club scarves Access to one exclusive Chelsea FC virtual event Access to all exclusive Chelsea FC virtual events Priority access to global CFC events Priority access to global CFC events Official signed Chelsea FC item This refreshed offering follows the launch of the new Official Supporters Club website, a dedicated platform created to help Chelsea’s global network of clubs stay connected. The website makes it easier for supporters to find and join their local club, discover club activity and share their passion for the Blues with fans across the world. Today, Chelsea is represented by more than 300 Official Supporters Clubs in over 150 countries, with new groups joining every day. From matchday cheering on the team, to local events that bring fans together, our Official Supporters Clubs play a vital role in representing Chelsea across every corner of the globe. The refreshed benefits and rewards mark another important step in the continued development of the Official Supporters Club programme, with more to come for clubs and their members.

news.title: Cobham Next Gen vs Bournemouth: How to watch it live
news.body_en: Cobham Next Gen kick off our Premier League 2 campaign this week and CFC+ subscribers can watch the opening game live on the Chelsea Official App and website. The Chelsea side competing at Under-21s level in the Premier League 2 will from this season be known as Cobham Next Gen, a name better reflecting the younger age profile of the top development side in the Blues' Academy. CNG begin the 2026/27 season with an away trip to Bournemouth in the Premier League 2, hoping to replicate our top-of-the-table finish last term. Here is how you can watch the match live... The game kicks off at the Wyatt Homes Stadium at 7pm (UK time) on Friday 21 August. All CFC+ subscribers can watch this match, and all of Chelsea's Premier League 2 fixtures this season, live on the official Chelsea website and the Chelsea Official App. You can get more details on CFC+ and sign up here. You can watch the live stream in our Cobham Next Gen vs Bournemouth Match Centre by clicking below or via the homepage of the official Chelsea website and Chelsea Official App shortly before kick-off. Ensure that you are logged in with your CFC+ subscription to view the stream. Highlights of the match will be available for free to all supporters on the Chelsea Official App and website on the morning of Saturday 22 August.

news.title: Vera Jones joins Watford on loan
news.body_en: Chelsea midfielder Vera Jones has completed a season-long loan to Women’s Super League 2 side Watford. The midfielder recently signed a new contract at Chelsea, committing her future to the club until at least 2029. Jones will now embark on her second loan spell, having spent last season with Bristol City, for whom she played 22 times. She has also represented England at youth level, most recently featuring for the Under-20s. We wish Vera well at Watford and look forward to monitoring her development.
